gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-plein: Tilt Neon bends tube-like, constant-width strokes into big lowercase letters with a splayed c, loud and commanding from the first word. Plein's moderate lowercase gives that volume somewhere to settle.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-spline-sans: Tube-like strokes that never change width give Tilt Neon its loud, commanding look. Spline Sans brings wide gaps between curve ends and stems, and that friendly openness is what makes the pairing work.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-asimovian: A splayed c and tube-like strokes of constant width make Tilt Neon shout from the page. Asimovian does the quieter work, its tall lowercase built from one width of stroke for steady running text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-basic: Zero stroke contrast, a tube-like line and a splayed c, gives Tilt Neon its bold, commanding face. Basic backs it up in sans-serif, low in contrast, with a gentle bump up to capitals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-carlito: Bars and stems drawn at the same strength, plus a splayed c, give Tilt Neon its loud, tube-bent look. Carlito, in sans-serif, handles tight, readable small sizes.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-matemasie: Open, splayed letters and one tube-like line make Tilt Neon loud. Matemasie closes its round letters to small entry points and leaves broad gaps between glyphs, and that open-versus-closed tension is what holds the pair together.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-mukta-malar: Loud as a shop sign, Tilt Neon never lets its stroke weight vary. And Mukta Malar, whose ascenders are compressed, can take a little more size in running text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-ramabhadra: The text face reads big and tidy, with a prominent x-height beneath Tilt Neon, whose letters look bent from tubing. Ramabhadra shares its big lowercase scale with the heading, and that is what ties them.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough reads with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, a flat, level look across the line. And beneath Tilt Neon headings, whose line holds its width, a full page of it should move along smoothly.
gen-gf-turret-road-fs-quicksand: Commanding round letters, like open parentheses, make up Turret Road. Quicksand adds tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs beneath that pen-like line, so the two feel related yet distinct on the page.
